title: Pepper-Crusted Smoked Brisket Flat
seoTitle: Pepper-Crusted Smoked Brisket Flat | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Texas-style pepper bark on a flat that slices clean and holds on the line
subtitle: Lean flat with bold pepper bark sliced thin for ten
description: Adapted from classic Texas pepper brisket flat tradition (BBQ Pit Boys, Weber): a trimmed flat gets equal parts salt and coarse pepper, smokes until 203°F, and slices thin for sandwiches or plates.

steps.title: Trim and season
steps.instruction: Trim fat cap to 1/4 inch. Coat flat with mustard, then pack evenly with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Rest 30 minutes while smoker preheats to 225°F.

steps.title: Smoke the flat
steps.instruction: Place flat fat-side up at 225°F with oak or post oak. Smoke until internal temp reaches 165°F and bark is set, about 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Wrap through the stall
steps.instruction: Wrap in butcher paper when bark color looks right and internal temp stalls near 165°F. Continue until probe-tender at 203°F, about 2–3 hours.

steps.title: Rest the brisket
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped flat at least 45 minutes in a cooler so juices redistribute. Unwrap and slice against the grain into 1/4-inch slices.

steps.title: Hold with broth
steps.instruction: Toss sliced beef lightly with warm broth. Transfer to hotel pan, cover with foil, hold at 170°F until service.

steps.title: Serve Texas-style
steps.instruction: Serve on buttered white bread with pickles and raw onion, or on platters for plate service.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Chop trimmings into chopped-beef sandwiches with extra broth. Reheat slices covered at 325°F until 165°F.

proTips: Flat dries faster than point—pull at 203°F, not higher.
Slice only what you need for first service; keep remainder whole until second pass.
If time is tight, finish wrapped flat in a 275°F oven while monitoring probe tenderness.
tonightSpread: Thin-sliced brisket on butcher paper with white bread, pickles, and onion.
Simple pinto beans for a classic smoke-night plate.
leftovers: Chop into chili for the next cold-night pot.
Reheat in broth on toasted rolls with horseradish mayo.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Flat is leaner than point but still delivers smoke-night credibility. Thin slices stretch across the hall and reheat without turning greasy.
mealPrepNotes: Trim early. Flat can stall for hours—wrap when bark color is right. Hold sliced beef at 170°F with broth; never above 175°F.
